emergency.notes: Tourist police: 1155 (English-speaking, available 24/7). This should be your first call for non-emergency issues.

travelAdvisory.summary: Exercise increased caution in Thailand due to risk of unrest. Some areas have increased risk. Violent crime is rare against tourists but does occur.

travelAdvisoryUK.summary: Most visits to Thailand are trouble-free. Be aware of the risk of street crime and scams.

healthcare.costForTourists: Private hospitals cater to medical tourists and are excellent quality. Clinic visit $30-80. Emergency room $100-500. Private hospital stay $150-500/night. Bumrungrad International Hospital (Bangkok) is world-class. Public hospitals are cheaper ($10-50) but crowded with long waits and limited English.
healthcare.pharmacyAccess: Pharmacies are everywhere and many medications available OTC that require prescriptions in Western countries — including some antibiotics and pain medications. Pharmacists often speak basic English.
healthcare.hospitalNotes: Bangkok has world-class private hospitals (Bumrungrad, Bangkok Hospital, Samitivej) popular with medical tourists. Outside Bangkok, quality drops significantly. Chiang Mai has adequate private hospitals. Islands and rural areas have very limited medical facilities — serious cases require evacuation to Bangkok.
healthcare.insuranceAdvice: Travel insurance essential. Private hospitals require proof of insurance or cash deposit upfront ($500-2,000). Medevac coverage strongly recommended if visiting islands or rural areas.

pharmacy.hours: Many pharmacies open 24/7 in tourist areas. Chain pharmacies like Boots and Watson are common in malls.
pharmacy.tips: Pharmacies are widely available, even in small towns. Many medications that require prescriptions in the West are available over-the-counter here, including antibiotics. Always verify the generic name of your medication. Bring a translation app.

recommended: Typhoid (for extended travel or rural areas)
vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for travelers. COVID-19 vaccination requirements have been lifted.

water.notes: Do not drink tap water. Drink only bottled or filtered water. Ice in drinks at reputable restaurants is generally safe (made from purified water).

healthcare.foodSafetyTips: Thai street food is generally safe at busy, popular stalls. Avoid raw or undercooked meat and seafood. Be cautious with salads (may have been washed in tap water). Cooked food served hot is safe. Watch out for spicy food if you have a sensitive stomach.

travelInsurance.tips: Thailand has excellent private hospitals but costs can add up quickly. Ensure your policy covers hospitalization, medical evacuation to Bangkok, and repatriation. Travel insurance with direct billing at Thai hospitals is ideal.

healthcare.qualityNotes: Excellent private hospitals in Bangkok and major cities (e.g., Bumrungrad, Bangkok Hospital). Public hospitals are adequate but often lack English-speaking staff. Private healthcare is affordable by Western standards.

medications.prescriptionRules: Foreign prescriptions are not accepted. Some medications available OTC that would require prescriptions elsewhere. For controlled substances, you'll need a Thai prescription from a local doctor.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Codeine is controlled. Some codeine products may be available with a prescription at a pharmacy.

restrictedMeds.name: ADHD medications (Adderall, Ritalin, methylphenidate)
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substances requiring a Thai prescription. Some may require a permit from the Thai FDA.

restrictedMeds.name: Medical cannabis
restrictedMeds.note: Despite Thailand's medical cannabis program, it is strictly for Thai residents with specific conditions. THC and cannabis products are illegal for tourists.

restrictedMeds.name: Tramadol
restrictedMeds.note: A controlled pain medication. Bring alternatives if you need pain management.

medications.bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English listing all medications with generic names. Bring sufficient supplies of prescription medications in original packaging. A Thai translation of prescriptions is helpful.

connectivity.simOptions: Tourist SIM cards from AIS, DTAC, or TrueMove available at airports and 7-Elevens ($5-15 for 7-30 days with 15-100GB). eSIM via Airalo or Holafly ($5-12). AIS is the best coverage nationwide.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Free WiFi widely available at hotels, cafes, restaurants, malls, and 7-Elevens. Quality is generally good in cities. Patchy on islands and rural areas.
connectivity.bestOption: Airport SIM card from AIS (best coverage) or TrueMove at Suvarnabhumi/Don Mueang arrivals. eSIM if your phone supports it — activate before arrival.

cultural.tipping: Not traditionally expected but appreciated. 20-50 baht for good restaurant service. Round up taxi fares. Hotel porters 20-50 baht per bag. Spa/massage 50-100 baht.
cultural.dressCode: Cover shoulders and knees at temples (required — many temples provide wraps). Remove shoes before entering temples and homes. Avoid wearing black to temples.
cultural.greetings: Wai greeting (palms together, slight bow) is the standard. Higher hands = more respect. Don't wai to children or service staff. A smile goes a long way — Thailand is the 'Land of Smiles.'
taboos: Touching someone's head (highest part of body, considered sacred)
Pointing feet at people or Buddha images (feet are lowest/dirtiest)
Disrespecting the monarchy (lèse-majesté is a serious criminal offense)
Stepping on money (has the King's image)
cultural.haggling: Expected at markets, street stalls, and with tuk-tuk drivers. Start at 50-60% of asking price. Not appropriate in malls, restaurants, or shops with fixed prices.

safety.lgbtSafety: Very tolerant culturally. Thailand is one of the most LGBTQ+-friendly countries in Asia. Same-sex marriage legalized in 2024. Bangkok has a vibrant LGBTQ+ scene. Kathoey (transgender women) are culturally visible.
safety.soloFemaleSafety: Generally safe. Exercise normal caution at night, especially on islands and in nightlife areas. Drink spiking occurs — watch your drinks. Full moon parties on Koh Phangan require extra vigilance.
safety.notes: Most tourist crime is petty — bag snatching by motorbikes, pickpocketing in crowded areas. Road safety is a major concern: Thailand has one of the highest road fatality rates in the world. Be extremely cautious on motorbikes.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: 60 days visa-free (extended from 30 in 2024). UK 60 days. EU 60 days. Australia 60 days.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: November-February (cool, dry season). Avoid May-October (monsoon season, heavy rain). March-April is extremely hot (35-40°C).

hospitals.name: Bumrungrad International Hospital
hospitals.notes: World-renowned hospital serving over 1 million patients/year. Full English services, JCI-accredited.

hospitals.name: Bangkok Hospital Phuket
hospitals.notes: Best hospital in Phuket for tourists. English-speaking staff, accepts international insurance.

immediate: Monitor Thai Meteorological Department (TMD) and DDPM flood alerts
Do not drive through flooded streets — Bangkok floods can exceed vehicle height
Move to upper floors of hotel or building if in flood-prone area
Follow instructions from hotel staff during monsoon flooding
after: Avoid contact with floodwater — leptospirosis risk
Check road and transport conditions before traveling

steps: File a police report immediately — get the report number, you will need it
Contact the US Embassy or nearest consulate: +66-2-205-4000
Bring the police report + any ID you have (driver's license, copy of passport)
Apply for an Emergency Passport (usually issued within 1-2 business days)
Notify your travel insurance and airline of the situation
stolenPassport.notes: Keep a digital copy of your passport in cloud storage (Google Photos, iCloud) and email yourself a scan before travel.

steps: Go to the nearest police station (or call 191)
Bring ID or a copy of your passport if available
Request a written report — ask for an English copy or certified translation if needed
Keep the report number safe — required for insurance claims
For theft: list all stolen items with approximate values
policeReport.notes: In many countries, tourist police stations are available in major cities — they have English-speaking staff. Ask your hotel concierge for the nearest tourist police.

steps: If involved in an accident: do not move vehicles if anyone is injured
Call police (191) and ambulance (1669) if there are injuries
Exchange contact, license, and insurance details with other parties
Document the scene with photos before moving vehicles
Contact your rental car company's emergency line
Contact your travel insurance's 24h assistance line
roadsideAssistance.notes: Traffic drives on the LEFT. An International Driving Permit (IDP) is required for most foreign licenses. Rental vehicles are available at major airports and cities.
